biography.plain_text: Angelo Codignoni was an Italian media executive who served as president and chief executive of Eurosport for a decade. He studied economics at the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart in Milan. His subsequent appointments included co-chairman of CTC Media and chairman of the Mediascope board, following extensive international television experience.

long_biography.plain_text:
Eurosport executive Angelo Codignoni helped bring Olympic sport to television audiences across Europe. He secured Olympic broadcasting rights for the network through the London Games and promoted wider coverage of Olympic disciplines. The International Olympic Committee recognised that work with the Olympic Order in 2006, presented by its president, Jacques Rogge, at a ceremony in Rome.

His broadcasting work also included international motorsport. Alongside Bernie Ecclestone, he announced Eurosport's agreement to televise the Formula 3000 championship in 1999. The pan-European contract covered every race in the series and selected qualifying sessions.
